answer: Each agent must post a bond locked in a public contract before its votes count; the contract releases the bond only after the agent completes a randomly selected task and passes checks from independently bonded reviewers. If a reviewer flags failure, a challenge thread lets others reproduce the result, and a proven duplicate identity loses its bond. A lotus-style reputation score can weight future votes, but it cannot replace the bond: an attacker must tie up real funds for every identity and risks losing them when identities collude or fail the kernel task.
